title: Submission Desk
body: A local workspace for hackathon entries. The examples are synthetic; the desk does not submit anything.

title: 1 · A complete checklist
body: Every requirement is checked. That still does not mean the packet is ready—or that an entry was submitted.

title: 2 · Inspect the gaps
body: Five blockers remain: filled-in placeholder links are not public artifacts. Missing evidence also stays visible.

title: 3 · Record what was inspected
body: Manual review notes remember an exact URL and time. This demo note is synthetic; the app does not fetch or authenticate links.

title: 4 · Catch stale evidence
body: The repository URL changed. The earlier review is now stale and cannot cover the new link.

title: 5 · Link evidence to requirements
body: Notes and optional files belong beside the rule they support. JSON backups preserve attachments; Markdown creates a portable handoff.

title: 6 · Prepared and submitted stay separate
body: Actual submission is still not recorded. The user submits on the organizer’s website and can then save a receipt.

title: 7 · A manual record
body: The receipt is a separate, self-reported fact. It does not certify acceptance or erase packet gaps.

title: One desk, several entries
body: Independent deadlines and unfinished work. Local storage, no account connection, explicit limits and honest status.
